subject: Clarify: evidence handoff and deletion steps after Oct 15 incident
messages:
From: Erin Wallace <erin.wallace@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Logs and evidence we need after Oct 15 incident

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the quick sync on Friday. Our security team has a follow-up: for our internal forensic review we need a clear statement of what logs Redwood retained after the Oct 15 incident, how those artifacts will be handed off to us, and what the deletion process looks like after we accept the export.

Specifically:
- Which log types (access, request, audit, model traces, KV cache snapshots) are retained and where?
- How do you generate an export and what guarantees (hashes/timestamps) are included?
- If we request deletion of those logs after review, what is the timeline and evidence we get that deletion completed?

Can you please confirm and point us to any export/checklist items we should expect? We may need a chain-of-custody for compliance.

Appreciate it.

—Erin
Erin Wallace
Lead Security Engineer, Acme Corporation
security@acme.com

Erin — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (CS) and Karthik (Security/Infra) so we can assemble a concise handoff. High level answers below; we'll follow with a technical export checklist and a proposed timeline.

Quick summary (high level):
- Default retention (hosted): request & access logs (90 days), audit logs (90 days).
- Enterprise/contract customers can have extended retention (365 days or custom) — this is config/contract dependent.
- Ephemeral runtime artifacts (GPU KV cache, transient scheduler traces) are not persisted to long-term storage unless request-level debugging was enabled; in those cases we will include only the debug snapshots that were explicitly captured.
- Export/handoff: we can produce a bundled export (compressed, SHA256 manifest) and provide a signed timestamp. Exports come from a locked S3 bucket and we can provide an HSM-backed timestamp on request.
- Deletion after export: we support certified deletion. Standard process is purge from active S3 buckets, remove from backup snapshots, and update our audit trail. We can provide a signed deletion certificate within 30 days of your acceptance of the export (shorter if you need).

Action items for clarity:
1) Please confirm which artifacts Acme needs (e.g., all request logs + audit stream + any debug snapshots).
2) Confirm whether you require chain-of-custody (signed hash + witness timestamp) or just a hash and audit log.

I'm attaching an internal preliminary checklist to show the fields we capture during an export — it lists manifest format and typical timelines. We'll follow with step-by-step export instructions from the Console and a forensic manifest.

Best,
Sean

Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Erin — quick operational details from CS on how we pull the exports. I'm including the Console paths and notes for the export bundle.

What we can export for hosted accounts (and typical location):
- Request logs (http/gRPC): stored in s3://redwood-hosted-logs/<account-id>/requests/YYYYMMDD/*.
- Access and auth audit logs: s3://redwood-hosted-logs/<account-id>/audit/YYYYMMDD/*.
- Error traces and debug snapshots (only if debug capture was enabled): s3://redwood-debug-exports/<account-id>/snapshot-<id>.tar.gz.

How we package it:
- We create a single tar.gz bundle containing logs, a CSV manifest (forensic_manifest.csv), and a SHA256 manifest file (manifest.sha256).
- We place the bundle in a time-locked S3 folder and generate a pre-signed download link that can be restricted by IP/expiration.
- For chain-of-custody we can run the bundle through our HSM to produce a signed timestamp (attestation.pdf) and include the HSM signature with the bundle.

Console quick steps (for your security team):
1. Console > Monitoring > Exports > New export > choose date range / artifact types.
2. Select "Include hash/attestation" if you want HSM timestamping.
3. Approve export; we stage and send pre-signed link to the email address on record.

Attachment: audit_export_instructions.md (text/markdown, 6 KB) — step-by-step with screenshots for the Console path.

If you want, I can schedule a short handoff call and we can run a dry run export to show you the manifest format.

—Monica
Monica Patel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Erin Wallace <erin.wallace@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logs and evidence we need after Oct 15 incident — tech notes

Erin / Monica — adding the infra/forensics perspective and a few technical caveats so expectations are aligned.

Technical notes:
- KV cache / model context buffers: these are in-memory on the serving nodes. We do not persist KV cache snapshots to object storage unless explicit debug capture was enabled for a request. If debug capture was on, the snapshot file name convention is snapshot-<job-id>-<ts>.bin and we include it in the export tarball.
- Model parameters & weights: these are not customer data and are never included in exports.
- Token-level traces: we store request-level traces only when "request-logging" is enabled for an account; otherwise traces are ephemeral and not kept.
- Backups: our S3 lifecycle keeps immutable backups for 14 days before lifecycle transitions; for enterprise contracts we keep longer-term backups per SLA. Deletion requires expunging from active buckets and initiating a backup purge job (this can take up to 72 hours for standard backups, longer for archival).

For the handoff I recommend the following minimal package:
1) request-logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz
2) audit-log-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz
3) forensic_manifest.csv (CSV with file list + SHA256 + file size + generated_by + timestamp)
4) manifest.sha256 (top-level SHA256 of the tar bundle)
5) attestation.pdf (HSM signature timestamp, if requested)

We have an internal ticket for a special export workflow used in incidents: INF-4578 (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-4578). That workflow ensures exports are created on a locked node, checksums are computed in a read-only environment, and a witness signature is applied.

Attachment: forensic_manifest.csv (text/csv, 3 KB) — sample manifest format.

A couple of caveats:
- If you require cryptographic notarization beyond our HSM timestamp (e.g., third-party notary), we'll need to coordinate a short window where we can provide a mirrored copy to the notary.
- Deletion certification: we'll provide a signed deletion certificate that lists the manifest hashes and the steps taken to purge. The internal purge sequence will be: stage deletion request -> remove objects from live buckets -> schedule backup purge -> verify zero-byte listings -> update audit entry. Expect 7–30 calendar days depending on backup tiers and contract.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Logs and evidence we need after Oct 15 incident — legal confirmation

Team — legal sign-off on the proposed approach with a few required clarifications for the deletion certificate.

Requirements for deletion certification:
- The certificate must include the export manifest (file list + SHA256) and the bundle SHA256.
- The certificate should state the exact deletion steps performed, the timestamps for each step, and the Redwood representative who authorized the purge.
- Certification must be produced within 30 days of customer acceptance of the export bundle unless the customer asks for an expedited (7 day) or extended timeline.

Operational note: please ensure that the attestation (HSM signature) is attached to the export bundle before we hand it off. If Acme requires chain-of-custody, include the witness timestamp and a copy of the internal ticket (INF-4578).

Attachment: deletion_cert_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 18 KB) — template for what we send to the customer once deletion completes.

I'll coordinate with Compliance for signature. Once we have a confirmed list of artifacts from Acme and their chain-of-custody requirements, Legal will prepare the final certificate text for signature.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
